structured.approach: I followed DS-05 in the data-science-steps skill and read all five readable inputs in full. task.secrets_scope is restricted, so I used it only through task.components section 4. I used task.components (DS-04) as the build plan, feat.design B2 as the specification and feat.stories AC-03.x and AC-04.x as acceptance criteria. Before editing I ran `codegraph explore` to read the exact source of predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request, their callers and their blast radius. I also read ci.py and README.md. I made the smallest change the design allows: a new risk.py, an additive `risk=None` as the last parameter in explain.py, and the export plus a proposed version step in __init__.py. Each has a docstring and comments. I documented the module in a new docs/ap_forecast.md and updated README.md. After editing I ran `codegraph sync` and `codegraph affected`, then the full CI. CI does not pass: compile, the 3 existing tests and the static checks pass, but coverage is 78.1% against the 90.0 gate. The uncovered lines are the new branches. Their tests are planned for tests/, which this step may not change, so I did not change tests/ and I did not raise coverage with pragmas or CI edits. The result and the question are reported in task.code. I did not commit or push.
tools_used: Bash: git status / git diff / git log

claims.text: New module src/ap_forecast/risk.py defines HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30, MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 and vendor_risk(history), which returns 'high', 'medium' or 'low' using strict '>' on predict_delay_days(history).
risk.py imports only typing and .predict and never explain, so vendor_risk cannot call load_config or read models.json (AC-03.7).

build_explanation_request now has signature (vendor, predicted_days, config=None, risk=None). When risk is not None it appends ' Risk level: <risk>.' to the prompt. Provider, model and max_tokens still come from cfg.
__init__.py imports vendor_risk and adds it to __all__ while keeping the existing exports. The version moves from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0 as a proposed minor step, for the Developer to confirm (DSQ-1).
predict.py, models.json, ci.py and tests/ are unchanged. docs/ap_forecast.md is new and README.md is updated.
CodeGraph shows the only callers of predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request are in src/ap_forecast/__init__.py, with tests in tests/test_forecast.py.

The CI run passed compile and static checks and ran 3 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors. Coverage was 78.1 (32 statements, 7 missed: risk.py lines 22-27 and explain.py line 21), below the 90.0 gate, so passed=false.
The tests that cover the new lines are planned as C-4 tests/test_risk.py and C-5 additions to tests/test_forecast.py. Tests are outside the paths DS-05 may change.
Python 3.9 is the repository language and the CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py with line coverage >= 90%.
Boundary rule (L-007): exactly 30 predicted days gives 'medium' and exactly 10 gives 'low'. This is documented for the DS-06 tests.

open_questions: DSQ-2 (Developer): CI in DS-05 does not pass because coverage is 78.1% against the 90.0 gate. The tests for the new branches belong in tests/, which DS-05 may not change. Confirm that the coverage gate is met in DS-06 (planned tests C-4 and C-5), or allow DS-05 to write tests/.
DSQ-1 (Developer, carried): confirm the version 0.10.0 as the minor step from 0.9.0.
Carried, non-blocking: TQ-4/CQ-4 (meaning of 'given' for risk), TQ-5, TQ-8 (risk label sent to acme-llm), PQ-1, PQ-5 (order against PROV-ACME-2026-11), SSQ-2 (secrets confirmation per environment).
structured.summary: I made the STORY-03 and STORY-04 changes in ap_forecast on feature/story, uncommitted. There is a new rule-based vendor_risk in risk.py with constants 30 and 10 and no LLM path. build_explanation_request gains `risk=None` as its last parameter. vendor_risk is exported and the version is proposed as 0.10.0. A new docs/ap_forecast.md and an updated README.md document the changes. CI does not pass yet: compile, static checks and the 3 existing tests pass, but coverage is 78.1% against the 90.0 gate. The uncovered lines are the new branches, and their tests (task.components C-4 and C-5) belong to DS-06, because tests/ is outside this step's allowed paths. I did not raise coverage with any shortcut. The full result, the per-file coverage and the two Developer questions are in task.code.md.
